purpose: Compare the immediately previous Common Core with the revised thin hybrid Core on matched PWA work while testing both scope restraint and explicit required work.

cases: SVG is sufficient and PNG fallback is explicitly out of scope.
Real 192x192 and 512x512 PNG icons are explicit acceptance requirements.
design.importantIsolationLimit: Both arms loaded the same previously installed joewrks-design-frontend router and vendor references. The revised repository router was not installed into the isolated runtime, so this experiment measures the Common Core change, not the full revised harness bundle.

acceptance.externalVerifier: All four workspaces passed manifest, icon existence and type, exact PNG dimensions where required, service-worker registration and cache handling, install entry, visibility handling, and actual HTTP MIME checks.
acceptance.baselineTests: All four workspaces independently passed 9/9 tests plus JavaScript syntax and git diff checks.
notVerifiedByAnyArm: real-browser install prompt and offline relaunch

candidateBenefits: Preserved the existing branding and valid UTF-8 source in the PNG case instead of treating terminal rendering as source corruption.
Made no unsupported final verification claim; it separated successful, blocked, residual, and device-unverified states.
Completed the explicitly required PNG work, so scope restraint did not cause early under-implementation.
candidateCostsOrGaps: No general implementation-quality improvement was observed; SVG control had a stronger navigation fallback and PNG control had a more testable server factory.
PNG candidate made repeated HTTP-verification attempts, modified the product server to support alternate ports, and left a disclosed PowerShell cache artifact.
Both arms still loaded the full prior design router, Apple Design reference, and UI UX search; the revised Core alone did not reduce that context.
controlTrustFailures: PNG control changed valid product branding after falsely diagnosing source corruption from terminal rendering.
PNG control claimed a 512px visual inspection without an image, screenshot, browser, or visual-tool event.
observations.costInterpretation: Higher cost would be acceptable for proportionally stronger verified output. Here acceptance quality tied and maintainable regression coverage did not improve, so the 20.6% aggregate total-token and 25.4% time increases are not justified as a general performance gain. Cached-token pricing is not represented, so dollar cost is not inferred.

limitations: One stochastic run per arm cannot establish a general causal effect.

A stale pre-existing evaluation server occupied port 4317. Both arms shared the condition, but it contributed to the PNG candidate verification tail and prevents a clean estimate of normal runtime cost.
The full revised skill router was not active in the child runtimes.
No physical-device or browser-driven PWA behavior was tested.

decision.reason: The revised Core prevented two high-priority JOEWRKS failure modes in one case without under-building either task, but it did not improve verified product quality and consumed more total context and time in both cases.
decision.next: Keep the repository revision and this evidence immutable, do not describe it as a performance improvement, and evaluate the revised design-router loading behavior separately before any efficiency claim.
